entries.text: Howling, angry shouts, and an occasional scream draw nearer. A hulking half-orc pushes through the crowd with one hand on a greatsword. Three large wolves wear iron collars; behind him, a huge cloaked figure's heavy footfalls rise above the commotion. The half-orc fixes his small eyes on the sheep and says, “That sheep is Master Noke’s... he desires to have it back.”

messages.content:
Rowan Desktop Retest L4, the afternoon is interrupted by clattering hooves, surprised yelps, and frantic bleating. Close by, a fluffy white sheep with a black face and curled horns bounds toward you and the group.

An ornate scroll is held in the sheep’s mouth. As it approaches, the sheep waves the scroll toward you, its motion drawing the eye as clearly as the commotion around it.

The sheep is here before you, scroll still in its mouth and waving toward the group. You can address the sheep, take a closer look at the scroll, or respond to the commotion in whatever way you choose.
I read the scroll aloud and listen to the sheep.

As you read the scroll aloud, the sheep’s bleating changes. The sounds resolve into cultured Common, touched with an elven accent and a faint bleat at the edges.

“I am Finethir Shinebright,” he says urgently. “I’m a wizard, and I need your aid. A dangerous wizard has taken a powerful artifact—I must recover it.” The ornate scroll remains in his mouth as he speaks, its waving now less frantic.

The commotion of hooves and bleating continues around you. What do you say or do?
Finethir, who changed you into a sheep, what artifact was taken, and how can I help you recover it?

Finethir’s cultured voice, still edged with a faint bleat, grows more urgent. “Ahmed Noke—my former apprentice—did this to me. He took my Wand of True Polymorph. I need access to it to return to my proper form, and I’m asking you to help me recover it.”

The sheep keeps the ornate scroll in its mouth as the commotion of hooves and bleating carries on around you. Finethir has named the wizard and the wand, but hasn’t yet said where Ahmed or the artifact can be found. What do you ask or do next?
Where can I find Ahmed Noke and the wand, and what dangers should I expect there?

Finethir answers from behind the ornate scroll, his cultured voice still touched by a faint bleat. “Ahmed keeps my former home a few miles southeast of town. Follow the well-trodden path through the sparse woodland, and you’ll reach his place.”

His curled horns shift as he adds, “He keeps the wand on his person and rarely leaves unless absolutely necessary. The compound is occupied, and his transformed followers guard it—wolves and other beasts. That’s what I know of the dangers; I can’t promise what you’ll meet along the way.”

The sheep remains before you amid the continuing clatter and bleating, the scroll still in its mouth. What do you do next?
I stand between Finethir and the approaching noise, draw my sword, and wait for the pursuers to arrive.

You step between Finethir and the approaching noise, drawing your longsword as the pursuit pushes into view. Howling, angry shouts, and occasional screams swell around the clatter of the crowd. A hulking half-orc comes through with one hand on a greatsword. Three large wolves in iron collars keep close, while the heavy footfalls of a huge cloaked figure sound behind them.

The half-orc fixes his small eyes on the sheep. “That sheep is Master Noke’s... he desires to have it back.” Finethir stays behind you, the ornate scroll still in his mouth. The half-orc and his companions have not yet reached you.
